newsitem.title: USA: Dollar hits 45-month high, buoyed by stocks, bonds.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hits 45-month high, buoyed by stocks, bonds.

text.p: The dollar surged Friday to a fresh 45-month high against the Japanese yen as U.S. stocks and bonds rallied, and on expectations that Japanese investors will snap up dollars when trading resumes in Japan next week.

"The bond market comeback and this stock market rally has really renewed, at least for the short-term, a lot of people's faith in the U.S. asset markets, so a lot of people are coming in and buying dollars," said Anjum Sayyed, a trader at Manufacturers and Traders Bank.

With volume approaching normal levels once again after several weeks of thin holiday trading, traders said dollar buying interest was coming from a wide array of players, including speculative accounts and corporate hedgers.

"There's a thought out there that when Japan comes back on Monday that they'll be buying dollar/yen, and I think, people are believing that will be higher on Monday morning," said Mark Gargano, managing director of currency derivatives at First Union National Bank.

In late afternoon trading, the dollar stood at 116.40 yen, after surging to 116.70 yen, its highest level since hitting 117.25 yen during the week of April 4, 1993. The dollar fetched 115.58 yen late Thursday.
Traders noted talk of stop loss orders to buy dollars from 116.40 yen up to 117.00 yen.
Japanese financial markets were closed this week for the New Year holiday. Trading gets underway again on Monday.
The dollar rose to 1.5650 German marks from 1.5430 marks.
Both U.S. stocks and bonds were strong Friday, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond steadying after Thursday's slide and the Dow Jones industrial average rocketing 90 points.
In late trading, the Treasury bond was unchanged to yield 6.74 percent. The Dow index was up 91.21 points at 6,533.70.

Bonds shrugged off a surprisingly strong November U.S. construction spending report and rose on talk the Japanese could be heavy buyers of U.S. Treasury securities when they return to the market Monday.
Traders said recent data sparked newfound confidence in the U.S. economy, spurred resiliency in stocks and filtered through to a strong dollar.
The British pound fetched $1.6895, versus $1.6942 late Thursday.
In other trading, the dollar rose to 1.3580 Swiss francs from 1.3465 late Thursday, but fell to Canadian $1.3710 from C$1.3761.
